Hikvision models come with resolutions from 2 to 8 MP and higher, support night vision, motion detection and face recognition, and suit homes, offices, shops, warehouses and industrial sites. Choosing a camera comes down to four things: resolution, low-light behaviour, field of view and where it will be mounted. For a home or small office 2–4 MP is usually enough — the image is readable and the archive does not fill the disk in a week. 4–8 MP is for places where faces at the door or vehicle plates must be distinguishable. Hikvision handles darkness with ColorVu, which records in colour under low light, and AcuSense, which separates people and vehicles from a moving branch and cuts false alarms. Outdoors the housing rating and temperature range matter; indoors, size and angle.

A camera on its own is not a system. It needs an NVR with a disk sized for the retention you want, a PoE switch so power and data share one cable, a power supply and cabling. We price the whole set and tell you in advance how many days of recording your chosen cameras and resolution will actually give — the parameter that most often surprises people after installation.

faq.a: The cost depends on the number of cameras, resolution, cable runs and installation type. We calculate the system for your site free of charge and prepare a commercial quote within 30 minutes.

faq.q: Which Hikvision IP camera should I choose for a home or office?
faq.a: For a home, 2–4 MP cameras with night vision are usually enough; for offices and shops, cameras with face recognition and a wide angle. Our engineers select models to fit your task and budget.

faq.a: Yes, Hikvision IP cameras support remote viewing via the Hik-Connect app. We set up access to the cameras from a smartphone and computer from anywhere.

faq.q: How many cameras does a home or shop need?
faq.a: A private house usually takes two to four: gate, yard, entrance, sometimes the back. faq.q: Why choose IP over analogue?
faq.a: Resolution and flexibility: IP gives a more detailed image, runs on a single cable with power (PoE), supports analytics and scales easily. Analogue is cheaper and makes sense where coaxial cabling already exists and a full rewire is not planned.
